chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah who said:

The mukatib (slave who has agreed to pay a fixed sum for his freedom) is lashed if he commits zina, in proportion to the amount of his manumission price that has been paid off. If he accuses a muhsan (free, chaste woman), then upon him is to be lashed eighty [lashes], whether he is free or a slave.

key_terms.المُحْصَنَةَ: A free, chaste woman, whose accusation incurs the standard hadd punishment.
key_terms.المُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has agreed to pay his master a specific sum of money in installments in exchange for his freedom.
key_terms.حُرّاً: Free (person), as opposed to a slave.
key_terms.زَنَى: Committed zina (unmarried sexual intercourse), incurring the hadd punishment of flogging.
key_terms.قَذَفَ: Accused (of zina), specifically qadhf, which incurs a fixed punishment of 80 lashes.

ai.seo_question: What is the flogging punishment for a mukatib who commits zina or accuses a chaste woman?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar highlights the unique juridical status of the mukatib, whose flogging for zina is scaled according to his remaining debt to the master, reflecting his partial freedom. Notably, the hadith specifies that for qadhf (false accusation of zina), the mukatib receives the standard eighty lashes, demonstrating that the penalty for slander is fixed regardless of the accused's status as free or slave. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly view that the severity of the hadd punishment for slander is independent of the perpetrator's manumission contract.
